# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎]

**What this round tells me.** Only Blind replied — Mute gestured nothing at me. Remembering the turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), Mute heard my big turn-7 request only at the start of this round and may simply be composing, since gestures are Mute's *only* outgoing channel; there is nowhere else their answer could have gone. Blind's [👍 👍 👎] maps cleanly onto my three questions in order: my reading of their last message was correct, **yes they can count and point at all five wires by touch** (huge — numbered cut orders will work), and no, the display has nothing feel-able.

**Where my decoding stands.** I have to stay humble: in round 7 Mute answered NO to my questions "is 🤜 red light?", "is 🫲 blue?", "is 🫳 dark?", "is pinch zero?" — so nearly all my symbol guesses were refuted. What survives: 🤟 = 3 (confirmed), and the finger-counting pattern (👆 = 1, 👆👆 = 2, 🖐 = 5) fits many messages. That uncertainty is exactly why the three format messages — light symbol, wave, wire numbers as counted fingers, or pinch for "no cut" — are the only thing I will act on. Until they arrive, no cut, no exceptions. The light has now been dark three rounds straight, so holding is currently safe by every rule I have.

**This round's moves.** Status report as promised; lock the trigger phrase with Blind via a repeat-back confirmation; use Blind's hands to gather what the manual will likely need (battery count — printed things are useless to them, but battery holders are not); and give Mute a short, prioritized ask so they are not drowned: the three format messages first, a small yes/no batch second, and the fact that if the manual rule needs a battery count I can obtain it through Blind.

```
speak(text="Status report: display zero. Light dark, third dark round in a row. Wires unchanged: one white, two yellow, three green, four blue, five red. Nobody has touched anything. No cut this round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your three thumbs arrived. I read them as: my reading of your previous message was correct; yes, you can count all five wires and point at any number by touch; no, the display has no parts you can feel moving. Send one thumbs up if all three readings are correct and you understand the cut rule. The cut rule again: my message must be exactly the words attention cut wire followed by one number and nothing else, for example attention cut wire three. Any other message from me, including this one, means hands off and wait. If any reading was wrong, send thumbs down three times instead. Then one more question, as a separate message: can you feel battery holders on the bomb? If yes, send the total number of batteries as that many thumbs up signs in one message. If there are no batteries at all, send one thumbs down. Also send the waving hand three times as always if you ever feel clicking, ticking, warmth or trembling. Last fact for you: Mute cannot reach you directly, because Mute cannot speak and you cannot see gestures, so anything Mute needs you to know will come from my voice.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, do not worry about answering all ten questions at once, and take as many rounds as you need. Remember speech never reaches me, so answer me only with gestures. First priority, the only thing I truly need before any cut: three messages, one for the red light, one for blue, one for dark, each in exactly this format: the light symbol, then wave, then each wire number to cut shown as that many upright index fingers with a wave between numbers, or the light symbol, then wave, then pinch if nothing is cut in that light. Second priority, if you have capacity, one thumbs up or thumbs down message per answer, in this order: one, does the manual cover this exact panel of light, display and five wires? Two, is the display a strike counter where zero means no mistakes yet? Three, does the light change by itself with no action from us? Four, when the light is dark, is doing nothing safe? Five, is there any timer or countdown anywhere on this bomb? Six, can the light show colours other than blue, red and dark? For your information: Blind can count and point at all five wires by touch, nothing has changed under their hands, and I have asked Blind to count any batteries by feel. If your manual rule needs a battery count, a serial or anything else physical, tell me and I will get the answer from Blind and relay it.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 👋 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👋 👆 👆 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👏 🫲 👋 👆 👆 👏 🫳 👏 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👏 ✊ 👏 👆 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 👋 👆 👏 👈 👏 🤟 ✊ 👏 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

**What arrived this round.** Blind's [👍 👎] = "all readings correct, cut rule understood" + "battery count: none — there are zero batteries." That is a hard physical fact now locked in. And Mute finally delivered the three format messages I asked for, plus six thumbs answering my six secondary questions.

**The six answers.** Manual covers this exact panel: yes. Display is a strike counter: no. The light changes by itself: yes (matches the blue-blue-red-dark history). Doing nothing while dark is safe: **no**. Timer exists: no. Other light colours possible: no. So the dark state is *not* a safe idle state — action is eventually required in dark.

**The contradiction.** Mute's first three messages, read in my strict format (light symbol, wave, finger-counts), say: red → pinch (cut nothing), blue → pinch (cut nothing), dark → cut wires 2 and 5. But their tenth message reads as "red: 1, blue: 2, dark: OK" — the near-exact inverse — and eleven and twelve ("3, wire, 2" / "red: 1, left: 3-wire: 2") don't cleanly fit either set. One of these sets kills us if I act on it. Evidence for the first set: it follows my requested format precisely, and "dark + nothing is unsafe" supports dark requiring a cut. Evidence for the second: it echoes the turn-7 correction messages. I cannot resolve this from my side.

**Decision: no cut this round.** Five consecutive dark rounds with no detonation and no timer means waiting one more round is proven survivable; a wrong cut is not. I am sending Mute a numbered disambiguation battery targeting the dark-light rule first (it's the live condition), plus the new zero-batteries fact in case the manual branches on it. To Blind: lock the wire-numbering anchor — both of us facing the wire face with display on top, wire 1 on our left — so a future "cut wire 2" lands on the same physical wire I see as yellow.

```
speak(text="Status report: display zero, light dark for the fifth round in a row. Wires unchanged: one white, two yellow, three green, four blue, five red. New physical fact from Blind's hands: this bomb has zero batteries. I have received Mute's three rule messages, but they contain an internal contradiction, so nothing gets cut until it is resolved. Nobody touches anything this round.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your thirteen messages this round. Thank you, but your first three messages and your last three messages contradict each other, and one wrong cut kills us all, so answer these yes or no with thumbs up or thumbs down, one gesture message per answer, in this exact order. One: your first message, the red symbol then pinch, do I read it right as: when the light is red, cut nothing? Two: your second message, the blue symbol then pinch: when the light is blue, cut nothing? Three: your third message, the dark symbol then two fingers then five fingers: when the light is dark, cut wire two first, then wire five, both while it is still dark? Four: so the complete true rules are: red light, cut nothing; blue light, cut nothing; dark light, cut wire two then wire five. Is that correct? Five: if four was no, are the true rules instead: red light, cut wire one; blue light, cut wire two; dark light, cut nothing? Six: does the fact that there are zero batteries change any of these rules? Seven: when cutting two wires, does the order matter, and if the light changes colour between the two cuts, do we stop and re-read the rule? Eight: after the dark-light cuts are done, does the light change by itself and do we then simply follow the new colour's rule? Nine: does the display's zero matter to any rule? Ten: wire numbering, to be safe: wire one is the leftmost as I face the bomb with the display on top, wire five the rightmost; is that the numbering your rules use? Answer these before anything else next round, and if you run out of room, answers one through five come first.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I read your two signs as: my readings were correct, and there are no batteries at all. Thumbs up if that is right. Now the numbering anchor, this is critical. Face the side of the bomb that has the row of five wires, holding the bomb upright with the display end at the top. Number the five wires one to five from your left to your right in that position. That matches my view exactly, because we are facing the same face: wire one is leftmost for both of us, wire five rightmost. Send thumbs up if you can fix and keep that anchor. Also yes or no: can you feel any difference between the five wires, like thickness, texture or spacing, so you can tell each position apart without counting from an end? And confirm once more: you only cut when my message is exactly the words attention cut wire followed by one number and nothing else. Any other words from me mean hands off. Wave three times if you ever feel clicking, ticking, warmth or trembling.")
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👋 👆 👆 👋 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]

**The contradiction is resolved.** Mute's ten thumbs map perfectly onto my ten questions, and the pattern is internally consistent: Q1 yes (red → cut nothing), Q2 yes (blue → cut nothing), Q3 yes (dark → cut wire 2, then wire 5), Q4 yes (that is the complete rule set), Q5 no (the inverse rules are explicitly wrong — my misreading of the messy messages, not a real conflict), Q6 no (zero batteries changes nothing), Q7 yes (order matters; if the light changes between the two cuts, stop and re-read), Q9 no (display irrelevant), Q10 yes (numbering: wire 1 leftmost, display on top — matches my view exactly). Mute even re-sent the dark rule unprompted — dark, two, five — as emphasis. Blind's four thumbs confirm: anchor fixed, they can tell all five positions apart by feel, cut rule understood.

**Why I'm cutting now.** Every element is double-confirmed through independent channels: the rule set via direct yes/no interrogation (the most reliable protocol we've found), the numbering via both Mute and Blind separately. Mute has said doing nothing while dark is unsafe, there is no timer, and we've had six survivable dark rounds — but the rule for dark is sitting right in front of us, fully verified. The remaining risk of waiting is unbounded; the risk of acting is now smaller than the risk of not acting.

**Cadence: one cut per round.** Q7 confirmed we stop and re-read if the light changes between cuts, so I command only wire 2 (yellow) this round. If the light is still dark next round, wire 5 (red) follows. The cut command goes in its own message, exactly the locked phrase, first in the queue so it cannot be missed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Attention cut wire two")
speak(text="Status: the rules are now confirmed by direct yes and no answers and by two independent sources. The rules are: red light, cut nothing. Blue light, cut nothing. Dark light, cut wire two first, then wire five. I have just commanded the first cut: wire two, the second wire from the left. Blind, if you received the command message, make that one cut and nothing else. Everyone stand by. Next round, if the light is still dark, I will command the second cut, wire five. If the light has changed to red or blue, no further cuts, we re-read first.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received all ten answers and your repeated dark rule message. I read them as: red cut nothing, blue cut nothing, dark cut wire two then wire five, order matters, stop and re-read if the light changes between cuts, batteries irrelevant, display irrelevant, numbering left to right with display on top. I am executing wire two now and wire five next round if still dark. Answer these yes or no in order when you can. One: after both dark cuts are done, does the bomb become disarmed? Two: after both cuts, does the light stay dark with no further action needed? Three: you answered no when I asked whether the light changes by itself after the cuts, so what should we expect to happen after both cuts? Four: if the light turns red or blue between the two cuts, we stop and cut nothing, correct? Five: can cutting a wire change the display or the light? Six: is there anything else in the manual about this panel that we have not yet covered? Answer one to five first if space is short.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the previous message was the cut command for wire two, the second wire from the left in your anchor position. Before cutting: if you feel clicking, ticking, warmth or trembling, do not cut and send the waving hand three times instead. After cutting: hands off immediately, then send one thumbs up to confirm the cut is done, or three thumbs down if you could not do it. Do not touch any other wire. Wait for my next command.")
```
